roles.definition: Artist is broad vocabulary for someone who creates expressive work through visual, written, musical, movement, textile, performance, or other media. The work may connect with kink without making Artist a power role.

roles.label: Performance Artist
roles.definition: A Performance Artist uses action, presence, staging, or the body as creative media. Kink themes may appear in the work, while participation, observation, and documentation still require appropriate consent.

roles.label: Drag King
roles.definition: A Drag King performs an intentionally masculine character through styling, movement, comedy, lip-sync, or other stage work. Performers may have any gender, and drag presentation does not define gender identity or sexuality.

roles.label: Drag Queen
roles.definition: A Drag Queen performs an intentionally feminine character through styling, movement, comedy, lip-sync, or other stage work. Performers may have any gender, and drag presentation does not define gender identity or sexuality.

roles.label: Writer
roles.definition: Writer is creative-role vocabulary for someone who develops text, narrative, dialogue, or fantasy. In collaborative roleplay, a writer may help shape a scenario without gaining authority over other participants.

roles.label: Poet
roles.definition: Poet is creative-role vocabulary for someone who uses language, rhythm, and imagery to express experience or imagination. It is not inherently a kink or relationship role.

roles.label: Photographer
roles.definition: Photographer describes the person creating still images, whether as art, documentation, or part of a negotiated scene. Being behind the camera does not create control over the subject or permission to share images.

roles.label: Videographer
roles.definition: Videographer describes the person recording moving images, whether as art, documentation, or part of a negotiated scene. Recording, storage, and sharing each require clear permission from everyone depicted.

roles.label: Model
roles.definition: Model describes someone who poses, presents clothing or art, or becomes the visual subject of photography, video, or performance. Being observed does not mean consenting to touch, control, recording, or distribution.

roles.label: Muse
roles.definition: Muse is relationship or creative vocabulary for someone who inspires another person's art, ideas, or expression. Inspiration does not imply ownership, obligation, or permission to portray the person publicly.

roles.label: Crafter
roles.definition: Crafter describes someone who makes objects, clothing, gear, art, or practical items by hand. The label may signal contribution to a community but is not a power or assessment role.

roles.label: Organizer
roles.definition: An Organizer plans or coordinates community gatherings, discussions, classes, or social events. The role carries practical responsibility for an event but does not make the person an authority over attendees' private choices.

roles.label: Event Organizer
roles.definition: An Event Organizer coordinates the planning, communication, venue, or logistics for a community event. The title describes operational responsibility, not universal expertise or authority over participants.

roles.label: Munch Organizer
roles.definition: A Munch Organizer arranges a casual social gathering, including venue, communication, and welcoming tasks. The role supports the event and does not confer authority over attendees beyond reasonable event boundaries.

roles.label: Host
roles.definition: A Host welcomes people and supports the setting, flow, and expectations of a gathering. Hosting responsibility is specific to the event and does not imply authority in private relationships.

roles.label: Facilitator
roles.definition: A Facilitator helps a group participate, communicate, learn, or make progress through a structured process. The role guides the process rather than controlling participants or claiming final authority.

roles.label: Boss
roles.definition: Boss is authority-themed vocabulary for someone who directs tasks, people, or a roleplay scenario. In a kink dynamic, any authority is negotiated and separate from workplace power or entitlement.

roles.label: Vanilla
roles.definition: Vanilla is relative vocabulary for interests, activities, or parts of life understood as non-kinky or conventional. People draw that boundary differently, and the term should not be used as a judgment.

roles.label: Undecided
roles.definition: Undecided is a valid way to say that a person has not chosen role vocabulary or is still weighing what fits. It does not mean they lack interests, boundaries, or self-knowledge.

roles.label: Not Applicable
roles.definition: Not Applicable is for someone who does not find role labels relevant or useful for the context at hand. Choosing no role is a complete and valid outcome, not missing information.
